content.title: Text That Reads Like Text
content.hook: The words on a page are content. CSS controls how those words are presented.
content.context: For this lesson, focus on three controls: font-size, font-weight, and line-height.
goals: Use core typography properties to control readable text presentation without changing the underlying content or structure.

content.title: Font size
Font weight
Line height

content.question: A paragraph is difficult to read because its lines are packed very tightly. Which property is the most direct place to start?

feedback.correct: When the problem is the space between lines, line-height is the direct control.
feedback.incorrect: When the problem is the space between lines, line-height is the direct control.

activities.title: Typography lab
activities.instruction: Complete the code challenge in the workspace, then run checks.

feedback.incorrect: Check the requirements and compare your code with the expected structure.

content.title: One property, one job
content.text: A useful habit is to change one declaration at a time while investigating a visual problem. If you change five things at once, you lose the ability to tell which change caused the result.

content.question:
Which property would you choose for each requirement?

“Make the heading heavier.” “Give the paragraph more breathing room between lines.” “Make the body text larger.”

feedback.correct: Name the visual symptom first. Then choose the property that directly controls it.
feedback.incorrect: Name the visual symptom first. Then choose the property that directly controls it.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: Senior habit: Treat typography as an engineering system. Change the smallest property that directly addresses the readability problem.

requirements: Screen-reader accessible code blocks and options
